scope: Native catch/finger contact geometry, including coarse-step sensitivity. Browser playback uses a separately projected and audited bake; this study does not qualify visible assembly clearance or source fit.
assumptions: Catch body traced from plate 181, rounded head compromised between plates 181 and 182; terminal finger surfaces inferred from both plates.
Upper holding face lifted 3 source pixels and its toe extended 2 pixels along the same ledge; lower heel moved 6 pixels right and 5 up to register with the fitted handle axes.
Registered model has a one-sided catch stop at zero radians; unregistered control permits -0.3 radians.
Catch mass 0.17, handle masses 0.1, inertias, friction and stops are diagnostic assumptions. The previous 0.25 catch mass is retained as a failed return-transfer control.
Contact layers separate the working arms from the catching fingers; connecting hardware and full visible-solid validation are not included.
The isolated release control applies a 6-unit torque pulse directly to the catch for 0.2 seconds; the coupled model actuates only the piston.
